accuracy.evidence: Arctic as an ice-covered ocean ringed by land and Antarctica as an ice-covered continent ringed by the Southern Ocean (National Geographic, British Antarctic Survey); polar bears, walruses, narwhals, snowy owls and Arctic foxes in the north and emperor and Adélie penguins, Weddell and leopard seals and wandering albatrosses in the south; penguins worded as 'almost only in the southern hemisphere, none in the Arctic' because Galápagos penguins reach the equator; walrus blubber up to about 15 cm (NOAA Fisheries) and polar bear blubber up to about 11 cm (Polar Bears International); huddling cuts heat loss (BAS emperor penguin facts), worded 'up to about half'; Arctic fox twice-yearly moult with a dark blue morph noted.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented ideas: polar bears and penguins live together (first prediction, wrong-pole feedback, p1, tags pole and south); blubber is fur or muscle (p2, tag blub); swimming hard keeps a walrus warm ('Swim harder instead' button, blubber prediction); fur makes heat (m3, tag fur); penguins huddle to hide from polar bears (huddle prediction, 'Huddle to hide from polar bears' button, m1, tag huddle); the Arctic fox is white all year (coat prediction, p5, tag coat); big ears keep an animal warm (build prediction, the big-ears feature, m4, tag ears).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpolaran is about cold and the two poles: animal cards dragged into Arctic and Antarctic panels, a walrus body whose blubber ring is dragged thicker in an icy tank with a heat-lost bar, six penguins dragged into a dashed huddle circle in the wind, coat swatches dragged onto an Arctic fox as the season flips from winter snow to summer ground, and six features toggled before a blizzard test. flagdesert is about heat and water, flagmigrate about seasonal journeys and flagcamo about camouflage in general.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees each effect first: a wrong pole card is sent back with where the animal really lives; the heat-lost bar falls from about 90% and turns green only once the blubber is thick; the per-penguin heat bar drops with every penguin that joins; a white coat on brown summer ground is rejected because it shows up; the blizzard test fails and names the first bad feature (big thin ears, short fur, sweating) until only warm features are chosen. The step text then names blubber, insulation, huddling and moulting.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with a tempting wrong option: 'yes, they share the icy poles', 'swimming fast all the time', 'to hide from polar bears' (alongside 'to keep their eggs dry'), 'white all year' and 'big thin ears'. Each is disproved in the task that follows and the reveal names the right option.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (where polar bears live, where emperor penguins live, what blubber is, why penguins huddle, the Arctic fox's winter colour, which ears keep heat in, how fur keeps a bear warm). Wrong options carry tags pole, south, blub, huddle, coat, ears and fur, each with its own message, e.g. 'Fur does not make heat. It traps a layer of warm air so body heat stays in.'

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 2.9 and adult 8.6 (family targets 5.0 and 10.0). Science words Arctic, Antarctic, adaptation, blubber, huddle and moult are each used with a plain explanation; insulation and camouflage appear in the adult key words.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: the two poles and their animals, why bears and penguins never meet, blubber, fur and small ears, huddling and the fox's coat. Adult: NC link and key words, geography and named animals with figures, huddling and moult detail with the blue morph caveat, six named mistakes and the lab steps. No filler pattern matched and the overlap gate passed against 642 Desert Animals.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light screenshots after Show me for each step: the two pole panels fit side by side with three animals listed in each; the blubber label overlapped the tank caption and was moved to its own line under the heading; meters on the blubber, huddle and blizzard steps were raised so the four-line feedback strip never covers them; coat swatches sit above the strip; the six feature chips fit in a 2 × 3 grid with the blizzard button below.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin: 'Arctic (north)' / 'Antarctic (south)' labelled with the current animal, 'Thicker blubber' / 'Thinner blubber' / 'Swim harder instead', 'Add a penguin to the huddle' / 'Huddle to hide from polar bears', 'White coat' / 'Brown coat', 'Add/Remove <feature>' and 'Blizzard test'. The canvas aria-label and live region carry each message. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.

sources: National Curriculum in England: science programmes of study, Year 2 Living things and their habitats; Year 6 Evolution and inheritance (adaptation) (DfE, 2013)

NOAA Fisheries: Pacific walrus (blubber up to about 15 cm) and NOAA Arctic Program: what is the Arctic
